name: Warehouse / distribution
summary: Bulk tilt-wall or precast distribution (32–40' clear) is one of the cheapest building types per SF; cost is driven by building size (fixed costs spread over more SF), slab/structure spec, clear height, dock-door count and the size of the truck courts and trailer parking. Data quality is good: Cushman & Wakefield publishes an annual model-building guide (2026: $78–$144 psf by size) and RLB publishes metro ranges, but the two differ in scope and basis, so the default leans on C&W for big-box product and uses RLB for the spread.

typicalSize.method: C&W models 109,200 / 476,400 / 901,000 SF buildings (e4). Typical speculative bulk product taken as 150k–1M SF with a 350k SF mid (between C&W small and medium models).

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Building SF per gross site acre at a floor-area ratio of ~0.35–0.48 (43,560 SF × FAR), typical for single-story distribution with truck courts, trailer parking and detention. Mid FAR 0.40 → 17,400 SF/acre, rounded.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Car spaces per building SF: ~0.3–1.0 per 1,000 SF for distribution (low employee density); trailer stalls are a separate line item.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Low = C&W 2026 large/medium model averages ($78–$87, e1/e2) and RLB low bounds in big-box markets (Dallas $75, Phoenix $85; e8/e9). Mid $100 = C&W medium ($87) uplifted ~15% because a typical 150k–500k SF bulk project sits between the C&W medium and small models ($87–$144, e3) and because C&W is an Americas average that includes cheaper Mexican/Central American markets; it is also the midpoint of the big-box-market RLB ranges (Dallas/Phoenix $75–$170). High $150 = RLB national median-of-highs is $228 (e7) but that is a generic-warehouse sample skewed to coastal cities; $150 ≈ C&W small model ($144) and RSMeans 2019 30k SF warehouse ($119–$131 in 2019 $, e12) escalated, and the bottom of Chicago/LA RLB ranges ($150–$155; e10/e11). Terrapin ($115–$185, e13) is a low-confidence upper cross-check.

scope.notes: Contractor price for core & shell incl. general conditions and OH&P, typical on-site work (grading, truck courts, car/trailer paving, on-site utilities, detention, landscaping) and a minimal spec office; excludes tenant office build-out beyond spec, racking/material handling, land, soft costs, off-sites and impact/tap fees. C&W category shares (e5) leave ~40% unitemised, consistent with sitework and GC/fees being inside its figure — verify against the full guide.

qualityTiers.method: economy ≈ low/mid (75/100); premium ≈ (C&W small $144 + mid) / 2 / mid for 40' clear, heavier slab, ESFR + more office; luxury 1.5 = high/mid for multi-story, automation-ready or high-power product.

systemSplit.method: Anchored to C&W 2026 category shares (e5): structure + enclosure 34–37% → 03 slab/tilt panels 22% + 05 joists/deck/columns 11% + 07 roofing/insulation 7% = 40%; architectural 15–22% → 08 dock/man doors, 09, 10, 11 dock equipment = 9% (less, because sitework is carried separately here); MEP 6–7% → 22/23/26 = 9.5%, plus 21 ESFR sprinklers 4% and 27/28 1.5%. Remainder: sitework 31–33 = 26% (large truck courts and trailer paving) and 01 general conditions/fee 10%. Judgment split — verify with a project estimate.

lineItems.name: Dock door package (9×10 insulated door, 30k-lb hydraulic leveler, seal, bumpers, dock light)

cost.method: No public unit price fetched. Built up by judgment: insulated sectional door $4k–$7k, pit-style hydraulic leveler $7k–$14k, seal/shelter + bumpers + light $1.5k–$4k, plus pit concrete/embeds; total $12k–$28k. Quantity: 1 door per ~7,500 SF (typical 1 per 5,000–10,000 SF for cross-dock/rear-load bulk).

lineItems.notes: Carve-out of the baseline; adjust count for door-heavy cross-dock buildings.

lineItems.name: ESFR sprinkler system incl. fire pump allowance

cost.method: Building-systems block gives $1.50–$3/SF for simple wet-pipe and $4–$9/SF for dry systems. ESFR in high-piled storage needs larger mains and often a fire pump/tank, so placed at the top of the wet-pipe range and into the dry range: $3–$6, mid $4 (judgment).

lineItems.name: Trailer parking stalls (heavy-duty concrete, 12×55 ft)

cost.method: 12×55 ft stall = 660 SF = 73 SY; paving block heavy-duty concrete $85–$170/SY (mid $115) → $6.2k–$12.4k; mid ≈ 73 × $115 = $8.4k + striping/bumpers → $9k. Quantity ≈ 1 stall per 10,000 SF (roughly 0.75–1 per dock door).

lineItems.notes: Carve-out of baseline sitework. Truck courts are part of the base sitework.

lineItems.name: Tenant office build-out (beyond spec office), ~2% of building area

cost.method: Per SF of office: between the vertical-building block tenant-improvement-basic ($45–$120) and the C&W 2026 Gen-1 office fit-out US average $162 (e20); low ≈ lowest C&W markets (~$108, e23) less a simpler warehouse-office spec. Quantity 2% of building area (typical 1–5%).

lineItems.notes: Usually a tenant improvement; turn on for build-to-suit.

lineItems.name: Rooftop solar PV (optional)

cost.method: Copied from _blocks/energy.json item rooftop-solar-commercial ($1,500/$2,300/$3,300 per kW, 2024). Quantity ~5 W per SF of roof (≈ 0.005 kW/SF) for a partial-roof commercial array (judgment).

lineItems.notes: Optional; many states/tenants now require solar-ready roofs.

pctOfHard.method: No industrial-specific soft-cost survey fetched. RSMeans models carry architectural fees of 7% on building cost (e12); big-box shells use repetitive designs, so A/E ≈ 3–5%. Add permits/plan review, geotech/survey, legal/leasing-free development admin, insurance/builder's risk and developer overhead ≈ 6–12% → 10–20% total excluding financing, mid 14% (judgment).

softCosts.notes: Excludes financing/interest and leasing commissions; impact and tap fees are site-specific and excluded from hard cost.

design.method: Repetitive tilt-wall shell designs carry lower design contingency than custom building types; 2–8% depending on design completion (judgment).

hard.method: Typical owner construction contingency for simple industrial shells 3–8% (judgment); higher for poor soils or heavy sitework.

soft.method: Soft-cost contingency 5–10% of soft costs (judgment, standard development pro forma practice).

perPrimaryUnit.method: min ≈ hard low $75 × 1.08 (lean soft costs); max ≈ RLB national median-of-highs $228 (e7) — a high-cost-metro bulk project with full soft costs. Values outside warrant a check.
